rules.summary: Opening, binding or passing /dev/uinput or /dev/input/* to a container or process (device flags, compose devices, direct paths).
Bind-mounting host input, X11 socket, Xauthority or Wayland socket paths into a container or sandbox (including ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/${WAYLAND_DISPLAY} spellings).
Device-cgroup rules granting major 13 (input) with any minor, e.g. 'c 13:* rwm' or 'a 13:* rwm'.

Loading or permissioning the host uinput route: modprobe/insmod uinput, chmod/chgrp/chown/setfacl/mknod on /dev/uinput or /dev/input, sg/newgrp input, systemd DeviceAllow, modules-load.d uinput entries.

Projecting a host display: inheriting ${DISPLAY}/${WAYLAND_DISPLAY}/${XAUTHORITY}, exporting or setting a display without same-boundary private creation, bare /tmp/.X11-unix or .Xauthority paths, xdotool/xhost/xwd, source set_var("DISPLAY"|"WAYLAND_DISPLAY"|"XAUTHORITY").
Writing the host clipboard: wl-copy/xclip/xsel, arboard/copypasta/x11-clipboard/wl-clipboard-rs/gtk::Clipboard deps, copy_text()/copy_image() APIs.

Fail closed: any value containing a shell expansion that cannot be proven statically, with no assignment-folding or proven-variable exception (container device/volume/mount/env/cgroup values, systemd BindPaths, compose devices, dynamic docker run/create image operands outside the -- position, option-shaped words after --, runs-on expressions, malformed shell/YAML/host-map, contract violations such as stale or duplicate inventory rows).

dormant-k-consumer.summary: Kernel-fidelity (K) consumer that is stopped on runner hosts in wave 1; removal is scheduled by the named wave-2 bead.

product-reference.summary: Product source that references host paths as data (policy constants, validation), never executed against the host in CI.

product-session-fixture.summary: Test fixture asserting on product session values (broker sockets, display env spellings) without touching the host.

guest_internal.summary: Occurrence only reachable inside a pfvd guest; the caller= entry point must exist, match guest_entry_points and reference the occurrence file.

product_clipboard_adapter.summary: Product clipboard adapter whose host route is gated off in CI; the occurrence file must carry the gate marker.

product_clipboard_adapter_call.summary: Call site of the capability-checked product clipboard adapter, bound by the exact occurrence line hash only; a new or changed call site is unclassified and fails until a human classifies it in review (#150 verification ruling).

forms: Xvfb :N started in the boundary with literal DISPLAY=:N and owned cleanup (trap/kill)
weston --backend=headless* with a generated socket under a run-private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR
private_compositor.summary: Creation and consumption must appear in the same test boundary (one shell file, one workflow run block). There is no free-form allowlist.

requires: individual source occurrence that literally carries both the producer X11 source and destination paths
product_session_capability.summary: Excuses the bare /tmp/.X11-unix destination spelling only on the same product-source occurrence as the producer-owned capability source; never file-wide, workflows, shell scripts or systemd units.

product_clipboard_adapter.adapter_caller: Calls to a capability-checked clipboard adapter are handled by the exact-occurrence inventory (#150 verification ruling): each adapter call site is a manifest row of class product_clipboard_adapter_call bound by the occurrence line hash (sha256 of rule + newline + stripped line text); a new or changed call site is unclassified and fails until a human classifies it in review. The adapter's own definition file keeps its product_clipboard_adapter row requiring the gate_marker in the occurrence file. The former optional adapter= field, its comment/string stripper and its import-binding heuristic are deleted (a text scanner cannot resolve call receivers or parse every language; exact-occurrence review is the sound mechanism). Detection is unchanged: copy_text(/copy_image( call sites and the listed clipboard libraries stay detectable everywhere, and only exact classified occurrences pass.
requires: gate marker present in the occurrence file

dynamic_image_operand.adjudication: pf-hwprobe#23 round 4: a text scan cannot prove a shell variable's runtime value.
dynamic_image_operand.option_parsing: Known docker/podman global and run/create option arities are parsed, so split values are consumed and the image operand is found reliably. An unknown option taints the command: the -- delimiter is not trusted, no positional operand is trusted as the image, and any dynamic operand in the tainted run/create command is dynamic_route (detail=dynamic_image_operand). Inline --opt=value forms for unknown options keep the command scannable. In the run context -t/-i/-d (and clusters such as -it) are booleans; --pull is string-valued for run and create and consumes a split or inline value (#147 review round 2). An unknown global option taints and its following non-subcommand word is treated as its possible split value, so a later run/create is still reached. The taint fail-closed applies inside run/create only: a non-run/create subcommand after an unknown global option carries no image operand and reports nothing.
dynamic_image_operand.summary: A dynamic docker run/create image operand (any quoted or unquoted expansion) is allowed only immediately after --, the end of options; otherwise it is dynamic_route (detail=dynamic_image_operand). A -- followed by an option-shaped word is dynamic_route (detail=option_after_end_of_options). Static literal images need no delimiter. The same no-folding rule applies to container device/volume/mount/env/cgroup values, systemd BindPaths and compose devices (detail=unresolved_value).

anchored_bind_sources.rule: A dynamic -v/--volume/--mount source is allowed iff it is anchored at a runner workspace root: it begins with one of the anchors, followed by end of word or '/', with no literal '..' path segment anywhere.
still_dynamic_route: whole-argv variables such as docker run $CI_DOCKER_RUN
anchored_bind_sources.static_sources_unchanged: /dev, /tmp/.X11-unix, XDG runtime dirs, Xauthority and Wayland socket sources keep their existing rules and stay red

coreutils_env_narrowing.rule: dynamic_route/unresolved_env_name applies only to container env options (docker|podman run/create/exec -e/--env/--env-file, compose environment). A coreutils env invocation running a host process is not a projection; the env command line is parsed like coreutils: options and their operands come first, then NAME=VALUE assignments, and assignment parsing stops at the utility; every supported option spelling is parsed: -u/--unset/-C/--chdir consume a separate operand or an inline = value, short-option clusters consume the rest of the cluster or the next operand for a trailing u/C, a bare - is the -i alias and not the utility, -- ends OPTION parsing only (GNU env runs env -- DISPLAY=x cmd with DISPLAY set, so after -- the normal assignment loop continues until the first non-assignment word and tokens after the utility stay ignored), and -S/--split-string operands are re-parsed as options plus assignments; only DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY/XAUTHORITY assignments inside the assignment prefix are checked, so env DISPLAY=$DISPLAY docker run ... stays red (host_display_projection/display_inherited).

shell_tokenizer.rule: malformed_file must not fire on shell that passes bash -n: command substitution $(...) and backtick spans inside double quotes are skipped as balanced spans (their inner quotes belong to the substitution), a backslash outside quotes escapes the next character inside $(...), and ANSI-C $'...' strings are single tokens.

clipboard_adapter_callers.rule: see typed_exceptions.product_clipboard_adapter.adapter_caller; design choice (#150 verification ruling): exact-occurrence inventory rows of class product_clipboard_adapter_call rather than any call-site text heuristic, because a text scanner cannot resolve call receivers and adapter calls are textually identical to direct framework calls

runner_label_map.matching: GitHub subset: a job's label set matches an entry when it is a subset of the entry's complete labels, or every label fnmatches one of the entry's label_patterns. Reusable-workflow calls (uses: without runs-on) are evaluated in the callee file.
runner_label_map.consumer_policy: A job carrying any host-input/display/clipboard finding that matches at least one committed host fails with host_consumer_job; a consumer matching none fails with no_eligible_host; dynamic runs-on fails with dynamic_runs_on.
